card.name: Verbs in old scholarly prose
card.fires_on: Auxiliary or linking words (be, shall, we, to, been) in formal, old-fashioned encyclopedia or scholarly prose. They come just before a verb of discussing or treating a topic, such as discussed, dwell upon or treat of.

modes.label: Be/been before a passive verb
modes.description: The word be or been follows a negation or modal in an authorial remark about what will or will not be covered.
modes.example: they will not<< be>> discussed further in this one.

modes.label: Authorial we/shall
modes.description: The word we or shall (or a nearby adverb) in a narrator's statement of what the text will treat next.
modes.example: We<< shall>> here dwell upon only the following two points

card.writes: It slightly favors words that start a formal verb phrase, but the promoted tokens are mixed and unclear.
card.plain: It fires on small helper words in old-style scholarly writing where the author says what will or will not be discussed.
